title: Delivery guarantees: at-least-once and the idempotency it forces

videos.script: Every subscription in Pub/Sub delivers each message at least once. At least once means sometimes twice. {{twice}} A publisher sends a payment and the answer gets lost. It cannot know whether the payment was stored, so it sends it again. Now there are two. {{retry}} A consumer adds a payment to a total and dies before it acknowledges the message. Ten seconds later the message comes back, and it is added again. {{crash}} Nothing reports an error. The totals are simply wrong, and somebody sends them to finance. {{wrong}} In this lesson you will make that happen on purpose, with a consumer that crashes halfway and starts again. {{demo}} Then you will fix it. A dedupe on the message id catches the redelivery and misses the publisher's copy. A dedupe on the order id catches both. {{fixed}} You will replay the whole subscription with a snapshot, and the totals will not move. {{replay}} And you will switch on exactly-once delivery, and see how little of the problem it covers. {{end}}
